summary: Added an item_price intent so callers asking 'how much is X' / 'what does X cost' get the price straight from data/menu.json instead of the generic fallback. RuleBackend gained _match_item_price with three phrasing patterns, hooked in after the FAQ check; menu.py gained price_text() (states both sizes for multi-size items per Kerry's clarification); dialog.py resolves the item and replies with the price or a clarification, never adding an order line. Also extended _QUESTION with 'price'/'cost' after discovering bare 'price of X' phrasing was double-counted as an order (caught by the pre-fix regression run). Order/read-back flow verified untouched via manual transcript.

summary: Fixed MUST-FIX review finding: RuleBackend.parse chained *self._parse_items(text) after an item_price match, so a price question naming two items (review's own example: 'how much are the egg rolls and crab rangoon') silently added the second item to the live order alongside the price answer. Changed the price-match branch in backends.py to return [price] only, matching clarification #2 (first-recognized-item price or fallback — never a silent order mutation). Added two regression tests to tests/test_price_faq.py that fail against the pre-fix code and pass after.
commands_run: .venv/bin/pytest tests/test_price_faq.py -q -k "two_items or second" (before/after fix, bug temporarily reintroduced to confirm tests fail pre-fix)
